input.text: These two towering gray buildings — the Drum Tower and the Bell Tower — were once the clock of Beijing. For centuries, city life moved to their sound: at dusk the great drums beat, at dawn the great bell rang — twenty-five booming strikes marking the opening and closing of the city gates. Inside the Drum Tower you can still see the original timekeeping instruments: the water clock that measured the hours for centuries, and ranks of great drums — the largest, a single hide over two meters across. The towers date to the Yuan dynasty — the older you look, the more impressive that is — and both were rebuilt under Ming and Qing emperors. Climb the steep stairs — they were built for duty, not comfort — and you'll stand where the night watch once stood, holding the whole city in one glance: hutongs breaking like waves around lakes to the south. In this neighborhood, time still moves slowly. These towers are the reason.
